title: Why the area is curve minus line
purpose: See that the curve is above the line between the intersections, so the area is the integral of (curve - line).

steps.text: The shaded region grows as you drag $k$ to the right. It is bounded above by $C$ and below by $l$.
Drag $k$ to $6$: the region closes at the second intersection, and the area reads $\frac{125}{6} \approx 20.8$.
Drag $Q$ along $C$ between $x=1$ and $x=6$: its $y$-value is always above the line's, which is why we integrate (curve $-$ line), not the other way round.

guide.what_you_see: The curve $C$ ($y = -x^2 + 8x - 5$) and the line $l$ ($y = x + 1$) from the question, meeting at $(1, 2)$ and $(6, 7)$. The shaded region $R$ lies between them, from $x = 1$ up to the dashed line at $x = k$.

legend.meaning: The line $y = x + 1$ from the question.
The first point where $C$ and $l$ meet.

The region whose area the question asks for; it grows as you move $k$.
The current upper limit $x = k$ of the shaded region.

interact.do: Drag the slider to move the upper limit from $1$ to $6$.
interact.watch: The shaded area and the live reading grow; at $k = 6$ the reading is $\frac{125}{6} \approx 20.8$.
Its $y$-value stays above the line between $x = 1$ and $x = 6$.

question_link.text: The shaded region is $R$. Its area is what the 5-mark part asks you to show equals $\frac{125}{6}$; the integral you set up (M1) and evaluate (dM1) is the area you are watching.

read_off: The live label 'Area so far' is the value of the integral from $1$ to $k$.
The label at the bottom left gives the coordinates of $Q$ as you drag it.
